chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:
I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

The companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah: 'Tell us, if you were to find a man upon your wife, what would you do?' He said: 'I would strike him with the sword.' He said: Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم came out and said: 'What is this, O Sa'd?' Sa'd said: 'They said: If you found a man upon your wife, what would you do to him? So I said: I would strike him with the sword.' So he said: 'O Sa'd, then what about the four witnesses?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, even after the sight of my own eye and Allah's knowledge that he has indeed done it?' So he said: 'Yes, by Allah, even after the sight of your own eye and Allah's knowledge that he has indeed done it, because Allah, the Exalted, has appointed for everything a limit, and He has appointed a limit for everyone who transgresses that limit.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابَ: the companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.بِالسَّيْفِ: with the sword; indicating violent personal retaliation
key_terms.بِالْأَرْبَعَةِ الشُّهُودِ: the requirement of four witnesses in establishing the offense
key_terms.حَدًّا: a fixed legal limit or prescribed boundary set by Allah
key_terms.يَتَعَدَّى: to overstep or transgress the prescribed limit

ai.seo_question: Can a husband punish a man himself if he finds him with his wife, or are four witnesses still required?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that legal punishment for zina is not left to personal retaliation, even in a case witnessed directly by a husband. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم affirms the necessity of legal proof and divinely ordained limits, showing that Allah has set boundaries both for offenses and for those who would exceed proper judgment.
